candidate.text: In the U.S. 2021 chart, online penetration among clothing purchasers aged 18+ was 77% before the start of the COVID-19 outbreak and 83% after the outbreak ends.
In the U.S. 2021 chart, online penetration among beauty/grooming purchasers aged 18+ was 57% before the start of the COVID-19 outbreak and 66% after the outbreak ends.
In the U.S. 2021 chart, online penetration among grocery purchasers aged 18+ was 43% before the start of the COVID-19 outbreak and 56% after the outbreak ends.
Amazon was the most common starting website/app for online beauty/grooming shopping: 38% of online beauty/grooming shoppers aged 18+ typically started there in the U.S. in 2021.
Amazon was the most common starting website/app for online clothing shopping: 36% of online clothes shoppers aged 18+ typically started there in the U.S. in 2021.
In the U.S. in 2021, 17% of online clothes shoppers aged 18+ typically started shopping at a department store.
Delivery was the most frequently used online-purchase fulfillment option for 56% of online grocery purchasers in the U.S. in 2021.
Delivery was the most frequently used online-purchase fulfillment option for 75% of online beauty/grooming purchasers in the U.S. in 2021.
Delivery was the most frequently used online-purchase fulfillment option for 84% of online clothing purchasers in the U.S. in 2021.
Curbside pickup was the most frequently used online-purchase fulfillment option for 34% of online grocery purchasers in the U.S. in 2021.
In-store pickup was the most frequently used online-purchase fulfillment option for 11% of online grocery purchasers in the U.S. in 2021.
During the COVID-19 outbreak, 50% of U.S. online grocery purchasers aged 18+ bought from at least one new website/app in the grocery category.
During the COVID-19 outbreak, 29% of U.S. online beauty/grooming purchasers aged 18+ bought from at least one new website/app in the beauty/grooming category.
During the COVID-19 outbreak, 35% of U.S. online clothing purchasers aged 18+ bought from at least one new website/app in the clothing category.

After the COVID-19 outbreak ends, 90% of the U.S. online grocery purchasers aged 18+ who bought from a new grocery website/app planned to continue shopping with at least some of those new websites/apps.

After the COVID-19 outbreak ends, 98% of the U.S. online beauty/grooming purchasers aged 18+ who bought from a new beauty/grooming website/app planned to continue shopping with at least some of those new websites/apps.

After the COVID-19 outbreak ends, 97% of the U.S. online clothing purchasers aged 18+ who bought from a new clothing website/app planned to continue shopping with at least some of those new websites/apps.

Among U.S. adults aged 18+ who bought from a new website/app during the COVID-19 outbreak, word of mouth was the listed discovery source for 49% of new grocery-site/app purchasers; social media was the listed source for 53% of new beauty/grooming-site/app purchasers and 49% of new clothing-site/app purchasers.
During the COVID-19 outbreak, 27% of U.S. households signed up for a new paid shopping program membership.
Of households that signed up for a new paid shopping program membership during the COVID-19 outbreak, 83% planned to keep at least one of those memberships over the next 12 months.
In the U.S. in 2021, 80% of households paid for at least one shopping program membership.
In the U.S. in 2021, the average household paid for 1.7 shopping program memberships.
In the U.S. in 2021, 64% of households paid for an Amazon Prime membership.
In the U.S. in 2021, 50% of households paid for at least one warehouse club membership.
In the U.S. in 2021, Walmart+ was the fourth most popular paid shopping program; the report says it launched 6 months into the COVID-19 outbreak (Sept. 2020).
In the U.S. in 2021, the average online shopper aged 18+ was comfortable sharing 6.3 types of personal data with online retailers to create an account/profile in exchange for personalized benefits.
In the U.S. in 2021, 67% of online shoppers aged 18+ had signed up for a retailer’s email list to receive a welcome reward.
In the U.S. in 2021, 57% of online shoppers aged 18+ had shared their date of birth with a retailer online to receive a birthday reward.
In the U.S. in 2021, 66% of online shoppers aged 18+ had signed up for a retailer’s loyalty program to receive rewards.
In the U.S. in 2021, 32% of online shoppers aged 18+ had signed up for a retailer’s credit card to receive rewards.
In the U.S. in 2021, the average online shopper aged 18+ was comfortable sharing 6.3 types of personal data with online retailers to receive personalized benefits.
In the U.S. in 2021, 78% of online shoppers aged 18+ were comfortable sharing gender, compared with 35% who were comfortable sharing browsing/search history on a website or app.

candidate.text: Although each is in a different stage of online adoption, all product categories analyzed — grocery, beauty/grooming, clothing — have experienced a permanent online shift as a result of COVID-19. Consumers aged 35+ will see the largest sustained growth in online penetration.
eCommerce discovery has forever changed as most consumers are starting their online shopping journey with specific retailers instead of search engines.

reasons: The evidence directly states that most consumers start online shopping with specific retailers rather than search engines.
